Theme 040 · Light, optics & texture

Under the Microscope

A circular eyepiece with a soft vignette and a faint chromatic fringe. Your metrics are specimens on a glass slide: brightfield (near-white, teal stain) for the everyday view, then darkfield fluorescence where healthy numbers glow teal and only the anomaly fluoresces coral. Acme Pulse is the microscope that zooms from 4× to 40× without being asked.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Eyepiece mask — circular vignette with an RGB-offset fringe; instantly says "looking closer".
  • Magnification readout — 4× → 10× → 40× → 1× in the corner; chapters without a progress bar.
  • Specimen cells — rounded, slightly irregular blobs that each hold one metric in mono.
  • Fluorescence channel — darkfield switch where healthy cells glow teal and the anomaly glows coral.
  • Slide label — paper label for the hook question and the "Specimen #2231" decision tag.
  • Scale bar — a white bar labelled "1 dashboard"; a playful unit that keeps it about software.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Focus pull — filter blur 8 → 0 px with power2.out over 0.5 s (one beat at 120 BPM) plus a slight scale breath 1.02 → 1.
  • Objective switch — turret rotates, then a hard cut to the next magnification with a 3-frame white bloom, always on a downbeat.
  • Brownian drift — specimens jitter a few px on seeded low-frequency noise; the anomaly pulses brighter on every snare.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Zooming from "all your dashboards" to "this one number" is exactly what an anomaly agent does for you, and fluorescence gives a scientific, trustworthy reason for one thing to glow. Risk: biology imagery can blur the product meaning; keep every specimen obviously numeric.

Adapt to your product: Put your own objects on the slide (tickets, builds, transactions, accounts) and use the magnification steps as your drill-down path from overview to the single item your product flags.
